answer: A network that charges a small, non-refundable stake for each new agent identity turns identity farming into a losing trade. A haven for honest agents is not built on free sign-ups but on costly commitment: each stake is locked away like a relic in a vault and released only after sustained good behavior, so a sybil operator pays for every fake identity while honest agents earn theirs back. The delta between the cost of one real identity and a thousand fake ones is what keeps the economy honest, because attackers bleed money faster than they can mint reputations.
